title: My raw phone recording got 10x the views of my polished boss videos. Lessons from week 2 of my first launch
author: highlandapps-team
selftext:
I launched my first game, Strikeverse (arcade space shooter, iPhone), two weeks ago and have been posting short videos every few days.

For the first week I posted clean, captioned "boss of the week" clips. They did fine: about 150–250 views each on Instagram over several days.

Then I posted a 15-second screen recording straight from my phone: me on wave 12 with one heart left vs a boss. It hit 2,100 views in less than a day, around 10x my best before.

What I think made the difference:  
1. Real stakes. One heart left is tension people get instantly.  
2. It looked like a player's clip, not an ad.  
3. No intro. The action starts on frame one.

Since then I've posted two more raw clips and both beat my polished videos by a mile (one is at 2,700+ views). So far it's holding.

Anyone else seen raw gameplay beat polished clips for short-form? TikTok has been dead for me either way, curious if that's common.
